question:
Arrange the venues of the following Buddhist Councils in chronological order (earliest to latest):

a) Vaishali

b) Rajagriha

c) Pataliputra

d) Kundalvana, Kashmir
solution_text:
The correct answer is b - a - c - d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct chronological sequence of the four Buddhist Councils is Rajagriha - Vaishali - Pataliputra - Kundalvana. (बौद्ध संगीतियाँ — कालानुक्रम)

 

• First Buddhist Council — Rajagriha, 483 BCE, immediately after the Buddha's death, under the patronage of Ajatashatru and presided over by Mahakassapa. Ananda and Upali recited the Sutta Pitaka and the Vinaya Pitaka respectively.

 

• Second Buddhist Council — Vaishali, 383 BCE, under Kalashoka, presided over by Sabakami. A dispute over the relaxation of monastic rules led to the first schism, into the Sthaviravadins and the Mahasanghikas.

 

• Third Buddhist Council — Pataliputra, 250 BCE, under Ashoka, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. The Abhidhamma Pitaka was added, completing the Tripitaka, and missionaries were sent abroad.

 

• Fourth Buddhist Council — Kundalvana, Kashmir, 1st century CE, under Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as deputy. Buddhism split into the Hinayana and the Mahayana, and the proceedings were recorded in Sanskrit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gandhara school of sculpture, patronised by the Kushanas, showed strong Greco-Roman influence and used grey sandstone; the Mathura school was indigenous and used red sandstone; the Amaravati school of the Satavahanas used white marble.

 

• The earliest Buddhist stone sculpture, at Bharhut and Sanchi, depicted the Buddha only through symbols — the lotus, the wheel, the bodhi tree, the footprint and the empty throne. It was at Mathura and Gandhara, under the Kushanas, that the Buddha was first shown in human form.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 give incorrect sequences. The common error is to place Vaishali first; the First Council was in fact held at Rajagriha, in the year of the Buddha's *mahaparinirvana*.

question: Which of the following statements about the Rath Yatra of Puri is correct?
option_1: A single chariot is used, carrying all three deities together
option_2: The chariots are built of stone and the same chariots are used every year
option_3: The festival is celebrated in the Tamil month of Margazhi
option_4: The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are carried in three separate chariots to the Gundicha Temple
solution_text:
The correct answer is The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are carried in three separate chariots to the Gundicha Temple.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Rath Yatra of Puri, Odisha, the three deities — Lord Jagannath, his elder brother Balabhadra and their sister Subhadra — are taken in three separate chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple, about 3 km away, where they stay for nine days before the return journey, called the Bahuda Yatra. (रथ यात्रा, पुरी — तीन अलग रथ)

 

• The three chariots and their names are:

◦ Nandighosha — of Jagannath, with 16 wheels, red and yellow

◦ Taladhwaja — of Balabhadra, with 14 wheels, red and green

◦ Darpadalana (Devadalana) — of Subhadra, with 12 wheels, red and black

 

• The chariots are built afresh every year out of wood, and are pulled by devotees with ropes. The festival falls on Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya, in June or July.

 

• The Jagannath Temple at Puri was built in the twelfth century by the Eastern Ganga ruler Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva, and Puri is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage centres.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chithirai Festival of Madurai is celebrated in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April-May), and commemorates the celestial wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, followed by the arrival of Lord Kallazhagar on a golden horse to the river Vaigai.

 

• Other major temple festivals: Pooram at Thrissur, Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik, and Ambubachi Mela at the Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Three distinct chariots are used, one for each deity.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The chariots are made of wood and are newly constructed each year, using timber of specified trees.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Margazhi is the Tamil month associated with the Chithirai temple calendar of the south, and the Rath Yatra follows the Odia lunar calendar in Ashadha.

question: In Carnatic music, what is the term for the improvised, rhythm-free elaboration of a raga that is performed before the main composition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alapana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alapana (called alap in Hindustani music) is the free, improvised exposition of a raga, performed without any tala or rhythmic cycle and without words, in order to establish the mood and the characteristic phrases of the raga before the composition begins. (आलापना — राग का विस्तार, ताल रहित)

 

• The principal forms of a Carnatic concert:

◦ Varnam — a short piece of fixed structure, sung at the start of a concert as a warm-up

◦ Kriti (Kirtana) — the main composed item, in three sections: pallavi, anupallavi and charanam

◦ Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi (RTP) — the most elaborate improvisatory form

◦ Tillana — a lively, rhythmic piece using percussion syllables, usually sung at the end of a concert

◦ Niraval and Kalpanaswaram — forms of improvisation within a composition

 

• Other Carnatic terms: gamaka, the ornamentation or oscillation of a note, and sruti, the pitch or drone reference.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In Hindustani classical music, a Bandish is the fixed, composed part of a raga presentation, with lyrics set to a particular raga and taal; the corresponding composed form in Carnatic music is the kriti.

 

• The Trinity of Carnatic music — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri — composed most of the standard kritis in the repertoire.

 

• Purandara Dasa is honoured as the father of Carnatic music for systematising its teaching.

 

NOTE

 

• Kriti (Option 1): The composed centrepiece of a concert, set to a raga and a tala; it is not improvised.

 

• Tillana (Option 2): A brisk, rhythmic concluding piece, frequently used in Bharatanatyam.

 

• Varnam (Option 4): A structured composition sung at the beginning of a concert, which encapsulates the essential phrases of a raga.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding rules of competition in certain sports:

1) In Olympic weightlifting, the two competition lifts are the snatch and the clean and jerk.

2) The boxing ring used in Olympic competition is circular in shape.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 is Correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. Modern Olympic weightlifting consists of exactly two competition lifts — the snatch, in which the barbell is lifted from the floor to overhead in one continuous movement, and the clean and jerk, in which it is first brought to the shoulders and then driven overhead. A lifter's total is the sum of the best successful attempt in each. (भारोत्तोलन — स्नैच एवं क्लीन एंड जर्क)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect. A boxing ring is square, not circular — its name is a historical survival from the days when fights were held in a roughly drawn circle. An Olympic ring measures about 6.1 m by 6.1 m inside the ropes and is enclosed by four ropes.

 

• Mirabai Chanu won a silver medal in weightlifting at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics in the 49 kg category, and Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal, taking bronze in weightlifting at Sydney 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Playing areas in other sports: a judo contest area is 8 m x 8 m with a surrounding safety area; a badminton court is 13.4 m x 6.1 m; a basketball court is 28 m x 15 m; and a volleyball court is 18 m x 9 m.

 

• Judo belt ranks run from white through to black; the red-and-white belt is worn by holders of the 6th to 8th dan, and the solid red belt by the 9th and 10th dan. Judo originated in Japan and was founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because Statement 1 is factually accurate while Statement 2 is not — a boxing ring is square, despite its name.

question: Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships. At which edition did he achieve this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Budapest 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neeraj Chopra won gold in the men's javelin throw at the World Athletics Championships 2023 at Budapest, Hungary, with a throw of 88.17 m, becoming the first Indian ever to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships. (नीरज चोपड़ा — बुडापेस्ट 2023, विश्व चैंपियनशिप स्वर्ण)

 

• He had won silver at the previous edition, Eugene 2022, which was itself only India's second ever medal at the World Championships — the first having been Anju Bobby George's long jump bronze at Paris 2003.

 

• Neeraj Chopra is the reigning icon of Indian athletics: Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020 — India's first ever athletics medal at the Olympics — and silver at Paris 2024. He has also won gold at the Asian Games (2018, 2023), the Commonwealth Games (2018) and the Diamond League final (2022).

 

• He hails from Khandra village in Panipat, Haryana, and has received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award and the Param Vishisht Seva Medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Athletics Championships is organised by World Athletics (formerly the IAAF) and has been held since 1983, currently once every two years.

 

• Gulveer Singh has emerged as India's leading long-distance runner, breaking long-standing national records in the 5,000 m and 10,000 m.

 

NOTE

 

• Eugene 2022 (Option 1): Neeraj Chopra won a silver here, not gold.

 

• Doha 2019 (Option 2): He did not compete, being recovering from an elbow injury.

 

• London 2017 (Option 3): India won no medal at this edition.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):

1) It was founded in 2001 and its Secretariat is located at Beijing.

2) India and Pakistan became full members of the SCO in 2017.

Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) was founded at Shanghai in June 2001, growing out of the earlier "Shanghai Five" grouping of 1996. Its Secretariat is at Beijing, and its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is headquartered at Tashkent, Uzbekistan. (शंघाई सहयोग संगठन — सचिवालय बीजिंग)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. India and Pakistan became full members at the Astana Summit in 2017. Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024.

 

• The founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The SCO's declared aims are political, economic and security cooperation, with a strong focus on countering the "three evils" — terrorism, separatism and extremism.

 

• India hosted the SCO Summit in 2023 in virtual format, and the SCO's official languages are Russian and Chinese.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BRICS — Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa — was expanded from 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE, with Indonesia joining later. Its New Development Bank is at Shanghai.

 

• BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) cooperation rests on mutual benefit and public-good-driven innovation, and is carried forward not only through the annual Heads of State Summits but also through STI Ministerial Meetings, working groups and the BRICS STI Framework Programme.

 

• Other groupings India belongs to: G20, QUAD, IBSA, BIMSTEC, SAARC, IORA and the International Solar Alliance.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The 38th National Games of India, held from January to February 2025 under the motto "Sankalp Se Shikhar Tak", were hosted by the state of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 38th National Games of India were hosted by Uttarakhand from 28 January to 14 February 2025, with the motto "Sankalp Se Shikhar Tak" — from resolve to the summit. (38वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — उत्तराखंड, 2025)

 

• Events were spread across Dehradun, Haridwar, Rishikesh, Haldwani, Rudrapur, Nainital, New Tehri, Shivpuri and Pithoragarh. The Games featured 32 sporting disciplines together with four demonstration events, and drew contingents from all 28 states and 8 union territories.

 

• This was the first time a Himalayan hill state hosted a multi-sport event of this scale in India. The mascot was "Mauli", based on the state bird, the Monal.

 

• The 37th National Games had been held in Goa in 2023, where Maharashtra topped the medal tally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Games are organised by the Indian Olympic Association in cooperation with the host state government and the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The first edition, then called the Indian Olympic Games, was held at Lahore in 1924.

 

• Related national multi-sport events under the Khelo India umbrella:

◦ Khelo India Youth Games — first held in 2018 as the Khelo India School Games

◦ Khelo India University Games — first held at Bhubaneswar in 2020

◦ Khelo India Winter Games — held in Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir

◦ Khelo India Para Games — the inaugural edition was held in December 2023 at three venues in New Delhi, across seven sporting disciplines

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 1): Hosted the 37th National Games in 2023.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Hosted the 36th National Games in 2022, at Ahmedabad and other cities.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Has not hosted the National Games.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): 'The White Tiger' by Aravind Adiga explores class conflict, corruption and social mobility in a rapidly changing India.

Reason (R): The novel is written in the form of a series of letters addressed to the Premier of China.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. 'The White Tiger' (2008) by Aravind Adiga follows Balram Halwai, a village boy who becomes a driver and then an entrepreneur, and is a sharp study of class conflict, corruption and social mobility in a rapidly changing India — the country of the "Light" and the "Darkness", and of the "Rooster Coop". (द व्हाइट टाइगर — अरविंद अडिगा)

 

• Reason (R) is true. The novel is indeed cast as a series of seven letters written over seven nights to Wen Jiabao, the Premier of China, on the eve of his visit to India.

 

• However, R is not the explanation of A. The epistolary device is a matter of narrative form; the themes of class and corruption arise from the content of what Balram narrates. A novel could explore the same themes in any form, so the choice of letters does not cause or explain the themes.

 

• 'The White Tiger' won the Booker Prize in 2008 and was Adiga's debut novel. It was adapted into a film in 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Last Man in Tower' (2011), also by Aravind Adiga, deals with the moral and ethical conflicts of residents of a Mumbai housing society facing the pressures of redevelopment and real estate — not with the colonial architectural history of the city.

 

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V.S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006) and Aravind Adiga (2008). Geetanjali Shree (2022) and Banu Mushtaq (2025) won the separate International Booker Prize.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Both statements are true, but the narrative form does not explain the thematic content.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: Choose the correctly matched glacial landform and its description:
option_1: Cirque - a long, narrow, knife-edged ridge separating two glacial valleys
option_2: Esker - a bowl-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley
option_3: Drumlin - a deep, steep-sided coastal inlet drowned by the sea
option_4: Moraine - debris carried and deposited by a glacier along its sides, front or base
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moraine - debris carried and deposited by a glacier along its sides, front or base.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A moraine is the unsorted rock debris (till) carried and deposited by a glacier. (हिमोढ़ — हिमनद द्वारा निक्षेपित मलबा)

◦ Lateral moraine — along the sides of the glacier

◦ Medial moraine — formed where two glaciers meet and their lateral moraines merge

◦ Terminal (end) moraine — a ridge at the snout, marking the farthest advance

◦ Ground moraine — spread beneath the ice

 

• The other glacial terms and their correct meanings:

◦ Cirque (corrie) — a deep, bowl or armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley; when filled with water it forms a tarn

◦ Arête — a long, narrow, knife-edged ridge separating two cirques or glacial valleys; where three or more arêtes meet, a horn or pyramidal peak is formed, as at the Matterhorn

◦ Esker — a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by a stream flowing beneath or within a glacier

◦ Drumlin — an inverted-spoon or egg-shaped hill of glacial till; a group of them gives "basket of eggs" topography

◦ Fjord — a deep, steep-sided coastal inlet formed when a glacial valley is drowned by the sea, typical of Norway

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other glacial features: the U-shaped valley, the hanging valley from which waterfalls descend, truncated spurs, roche moutonnée, crevasses and the outwash plain beyond the terminal moraine.

 

• Landforms of underground water in limestone regions (karst topography) include stalactites, which grow downward from the cave roof as dripping water deposits calcium carbonate; stalagmites, which grow upward from the cave floor where the drops fall; and pillars, formed where the two join.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: A knife-edged ridge is an arête, not a cirque.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The bowl-shaped hollow at a valley head is a cirque, not an esker.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: A drowned glacial valley on a coast is a fjord, not a drumlin.

question: The NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) system provides its Standard Positioning Service over India and up to what distance beyond its borders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,500 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NavIC, formerly the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), provides positioning, navigation and timing services over India and a region extending about 1,500 km beyond its borders. (नाविक — भारत एवं सीमाओं से 1,500 किमी तक)

 

• It is an independent, indigenous regional navigation system developed by ISRO, with a constellation of seven satellites — three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit.

 

• NavIC offers two services: the Standard Positioning Service (SPS) for civilian users, with a position accuracy better than 20 metres and timing accuracy better than 50 nanoseconds, and a Restricted Service (RS) for authorised users.

 

• The first satellite of the series, IRNSS-1A, was launched in 2013. The second-generation satellites are designated NVS; NVS-01 was launched in 2023 and NVS-02 aboard GSLV-F15 in January 2025, both intended to strengthen India's navigation constellation by providing precise position and timing data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The world's global navigation satellite systems are GPS (United States), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (European Union) and BeiDou (China). NavIC (India) and QZSS (Japan) are regional systems.

 

• GAGAN — GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation — is a joint ISRO and Airports Authority of India project that improves the accuracy of GPS signals for civil aviation over the Indian region.

 

NOTE

 

• 500 km (Option 1), 1,000 km (Option 2) and 2,000 km (Option 4) are incorrect. The service area specified for NavIC is India plus a region extending 1,500 km beyond its boundaries.

question:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The density of population is not uniform across the states of India.

Reason (R): Density of population is calculated as the number of persons living per square kilometre of area.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. Population density varies enormously across India. As per Census 2011, the national average was 382 persons per sq km, while Bihar recorded 1,106 and Arunachal Pradesh only 17. Among Union Territories, Delhi recorded 11,320. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — राज्यों में असमान)

 

• Reason (R) is true. Density of population is indeed defined as the number of persons per square kilometre, obtained by dividing total population by total land area.

 

• However, R is not the explanation of A. R merely gives the definition of the measure; it does not explain why the values differ from state to state. The actual causes of uneven density are geographical factors (relief, climate, soil fertility, availability of water), economic factors (industrialisation, urbanisation, transport) and social and historical factors (settlement patterns, migration).

 

• Thus the fertile alluvial plains of the Ganga and the deltas support dense populations, while the Himalayas, the Thar Desert and the north-eastern hills remain sparsely populated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Population growth can be measured both in absolute numbers — the difference between the population at two points of time — and as a percentage change per year. Absolute numbers alone are not sufficient for comparison between regions of different size; the percentage rate is needed for meaningful comparison.

 

• Arithmetic density is persons per unit of total area, while physiological density is persons per unit of cultivable land — a more meaningful measure for an agrarian economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The definition of density does not explain the variation in its values.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question:
Read the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India:

1. The Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President.

2. The Election Commission is provided for under Article 324 of the Constitution.

3. The Chief Election Commissioner may be removed from office by the President at his own discretion.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President. (मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त — राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नियुक्त)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324, which vests in it the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. The CEC cannot be removed at the President's discretion. He can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court — that is, by an order of the President following an address by both Houses of Parliament passed by a special majority on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The other Election Commissioners may be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.

 

• The Commission was a single-member body from 1950 until 1989, and has been a three-member body since 1993. The CEC and Election Commissioners hold office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other constitutional bodies include the Comptroller and Auditor General (Article 148), the Union Public Service Commission (Article 315), the Finance Commission (Article 280), the Attorney General (Article 76) and the GST Council (Article 279A).

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed by the President under Article 148 and holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier — so the CAG's term is not limited to a flat five years.

 

• Sukumar Sen was India's first Chief Election Commissioner. National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January, the foundation day of the Commission.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each includes Statement 3, which wrongly suggests that the CEC serves at the discretion of the President. The security of tenure given to the CEC is a deliberate safeguard of the Commission's independence.

question: Which cell organelle is chiefly responsible for the synthesis of lipids and for detoxification in the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks ribosomes on its surface and is the principal site of lipid and steroid synthesis, of the detoxification of drugs and poisons — especially in liver cells — and of the storage and release of calcium ions in muscle cells. (चिकनी अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका — लिपिड संश्लेषण एवं विषहरण)

 

• The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is studded with ribosomes and is the site of the synthesis and initial processing of proteins destined for secretion or for membranes.

 

• The endoplasmic reticulum as a whole forms an interconnected network of membranous tubules continuous with the nuclear membrane, and serves as the cell's transport and manufacturing system. It is present only in eukaryotic cells.

 

• The Golgi apparatus receives material from the ER and carries out the modification, sorting and packaging of proteins and lipids into vesicles for dispatch — which is why it is called the "post office" of the cell. It also forms lysosomes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nicknames of cell organelles frequently asked in examinations:

◦ Mitochondrion — powerhouse of the cell; the site of ATP production

◦ Ribosome — protein factory

◦ Lysosome — suicide bag; carries out intracellular digestion

◦ Golgi apparatus — post office of the cell

◦ Nucleus — control centre, containing the DNA

◦ Chloroplast — the kitchen of the cell, in plants

 

• Plant cells additionally possess a cell wall of cellulose, plastids and a large central vacuole.

 

NOTE

 

• The rough endoplasmic reticulum (Option 1): Bears ribosomes and is concerned with protein synthesis, not lipid synthesis.

 

• The Golgi apparatus (Option 2): Modifies, packages and dispatches proteins and lipids; it does not synthesise them from scratch.

 

• The lysosome (Option 3): Contains hydrolytic enzymes for digesting worn-out organelles and foreign material.

question: A Constitution Amendment Bill under Article 368 must be passed in each House of Parliament by which majority?
option_1: A simple majority of the members present and voting
option_2: A majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting
option_3: Three-fourths of the total membership of the House
option_4: Two-thirds of the total membership of the House
solution_text:
The correct answer is A majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 368 provides that a Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed in each House separately by a special majority — that is, by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. (अनुच्छेद 368 — विशेष बहुमत)

 

• There is no provision for a joint sitting in the case of a Constitution Amendment Bill; each House must pass it independently. The Bill may be introduced in either House, by a Minister or a private member, and does not require the prior recommendation of the President. Once passed, the President must give assent — this was made obligatory by the 24th Amendment.

 

• Certain provisions additionally require ratification by the legislatures of not less than half the States, by a simple majority. These include the election of the President, the extent of the executive power of the Union and the States, the Supreme Court and High Courts, the distribution of legislative powers, any of the Lists in the Seventh Schedule, the representation of States in Parliament, and Article 368 itself.

 

• Some provisions can be amended by a simple majority outside the scope of Article 368 — for example the creation of new States, the abolition or creation of Legislative Councils, and citizenship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The basic structure doctrine, laid down in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), holds that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 does not extend to destroying or altering the basic structure of the Constitution.

 

• The procedure for amendment was borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa. India's amendment procedure is described as partly rigid and partly flexible.

 

• Under Article 279A, decisions of the GST Council require a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting — a different threshold, often confused with the amendment majority.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: A simple majority suffices only for those provisions that lie outside Article 368.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: The Constitution requires a two-thirds majority of those present and voting, coupled with a majority of the total membership — not a fixed two-thirds or three-fourths of the total membership.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the position of a Money Bill under Article 110 of the Constitution?
option_1: It may be introduced in either House and must be passed by both Houses in identical terms
option_2: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President, and the Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations, within fourteen days
option_3: It can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha, which alone can reject it
option_4: It requires the prior assent of the Governor of every State before introduction
solution_text:
The correct answer is It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President, and the Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations, within fourteen days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 and can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the recommendation of the President. (धन विधेयक — अनुच्छेद 110)

 

• After the Lok Sabha passes it, the Bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, which has restricted powers: it may only make recommendations, and must return the Bill within fourteen days. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject any or all of those recommendations. If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Bill within fourteen days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses.

 

• There is therefore no provision for a joint sitting on a Money Bill, since a deadlock cannot arise.

 

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and his decision is final and cannot ordinarily be questioned.

 

• A Money Bill deals only with matters listed in Article 110(1) — the imposition or regulation of taxes, government borrowing, the Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund, appropriation of money, and related matters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not every Financial Bill is a Money Bill. Financial Bills of Category I also require the President's recommendation and can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but the Rajya Sabha has full powers over them.

 

• Under Article 255, an act done without the prior recommendation or previous sanction required by the Constitution does not invalidate the resulting law, provided that assent has been given by the Governor, or by the President, as the case may be. It is therefore a curative provision.

 

• The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration, since it is introduced only on his own recommendation.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: That describes an Ordinary Bill, which may originate in either House.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Rajya Sabha can neither introduce nor reject a Money Bill.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The assent of State Governors has no role in Union legislation.

question: When a ray of light travelling in a denser medium strikes the boundary of a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, which phenomenon takes place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Total internal reflection.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Total internal reflection (TIR) occurs when light travelling from a denser medium to a rarer medium strikes the boundary at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle. The light is then completely reflected back into the denser medium, with no refracted ray at all. (पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन)

 

• The two essential conditions for TIR are:

◦ light must travel from a denser to a rarer medium

◦ the angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle for that pair of media

 

• The critical angle is the angle of incidence for which the angle of refraction is exactly 90°. For a water-air boundary it is about 48.6°, and for a glass-air boundary about 42°.

 

• Everyday examples of TIR: the working of optical fibres, which carry signals over long distances with negligible loss; the sparkle (brilliance) of a diamond, which has a very small critical angle of about 24°; the mirage seen on hot roads; and the use of totally reflecting prisms in periscopes and binoculars.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• When light passes from one medium into another, its speed and wavelength change, but its frequency remains constant, because frequency is determined by the source and not by the medium. This is the reason the colour of light does not change on entering glass or water.

 

• Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in the medium; and Snell's law states that n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r.

 

• Dispersion — the splitting of white light into its constituent colours by a prism — occurs because different colours travel at different speeds in the medium; violet is deviated most and red least.

 

NOTE

 

• Refraction (Option 1): Occurs when the angle of incidence is less than the critical angle; part of the light then enters the second medium.

 

• Dispersion (Option 2): The separation of white light into its component colours, as in a rainbow.

 

• Diffraction (Option 3): The bending of light around the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow aperture.

question: Which of the following has been introduced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, as a form of punishment for the first time in Indian criminal law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Community service.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860, has for the first time in Indian criminal law introduced "community service" as a form of punishment. (भारतीय न्याय संहिता — सामुदायिक सेवा एक दंड के रूप में)

 

• Community service may be imposed for certain petty offences, such as attempting suicide to compel a public servant, theft of property of small value on return of the property, appearing in public in a state of intoxication and causing annoyance, defamation, and non-appearance in response to a proclamation.

 

• The punishments recognised under the BNS are therefore: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous or simple), forfeiture of property, fine and community service.

 

• The BNS has 358 sections, against 511 in the old IPC. It also introduces specific offences of organised crime, terrorism, petty organised crime and snatching, and replaces the offence of sedition with an offence relating to acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three new criminal laws came into force on 1 July 2024:

◦ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860

◦ Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

◦ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872

 

• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam was framed to align the law of evidence with advances in forensic science and digital technology, giving electronic and digital records the status of primary evidence and permitting evidence to be recorded by audio-video electronic means.

 

NOTE

 

• Solitary confinement (Option 1): Was already provided for under the old IPC and is therefore not new.

 

• Transportation for life (Option 2): An old colonial punishment that was abolished in 1955 and replaced by imprisonment for life.

 

• Forfeiture of property (Option 3): Existed as a punishment under the IPC as well, and is carried over into the BNS.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India.

Reason (R): It is conferred only on persons who have distinguished themselves in the field of the arts.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India, instituted in 1954. (भारत रत्न — भारत का सर्वोच्च नागरिक सम्मान)

 

• Reason (R) is false. The award is not confined to the arts. It is conferred for exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour. The original scope covered art, literature, science and public service; it was widened in 2011 to include any field, which is how sportspersons became eligible.

 

• Not more than three Bharat Ratna awards may be conferred in a year. The award carries no monetary grant; the recipient receives a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a peepal-leaf shaped medallion. It confers no title and cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to the recipient's name.

 

• The first recipients in 1954 were Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari and Dr. C.V. Raman. Sachin Tendulkar became the first sportsperson and the youngest recipient in 2014. Mother Teresa, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and Nelson Mandela are among the recipients who were not Indian-born citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The order of precedence of India's civilian awards is Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri. The Padma awards were also instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day.

 

• The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar, instituted in 2024, is the national award for science, given in four categories — Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar and Vigyan Team. It is administered by the Ministry of Science and Technology, not the Ministry of Culture, and is conferred on National Technology Day, 11 May.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 2 are incorrect: They both require R to be true, whereas the Bharat Ratna is expressly open to any field of human endeavour.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The Assertion is factually accurate.

question: The Human Development Index (HDI), published by the UNDP, is a composite measure of which three dimensions?
option_1: Health, education and standard of living
option_4: Health, security and access to technology
solution_text:
The correct answer is Health, education and standard of living.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite index of three dimensions — a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living, commonly stated as health, education and standard of living. (मानव विकास सूचकांक — स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा एवं जीवन स्तर)

 

• The indicators used are:

◦ Health — life expectancy at birth

◦ Education — mean years of schooling for adults aged 25 and above, and expected years of schooling for children entering school

◦ Standard of living — Gross National Income (GNI) per capita at purchasing power parity

 

• The HDI is published in the annual Human Development Report of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), first issued in 1990. It was devised by the Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq with the Indian economist Amartya Sen.

 

• HDI values run from 0 to 1, and countries are graded as low, medium, high and very high human development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The UNDP also publishes the Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI), the Gender Inequality Index (GII), the Gender Development Index (GDI) and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

 

• The Global Gender Gap Report, published by the World Economic Forum since 2006, measures disparities between genders across four key dimensions — Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Iceland has topped it every year since 2009.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Income, employment and price stability are macroeconomic indicators, not the HDI dimensions.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: These are broad policy domains, not the composition of the HDI.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Access to technology is measured by other indices such as the Network Readiness Index, not by the HDI.

question: Kalaripayattu, regarded as one of the oldest martial art forms in the world, originated in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalaripayattu originated in Kerala and is widely regarded as one of the oldest surviving martial art forms in the world. Its name comes from kalari, the training arena, and payattu, meaning practice or exercise. (कलरीपयट्टू — केरल)

 

• It combines strikes, kicks, grappling, weaponry (including the urumi, a flexible sword), preset forms and healing methods, and is closely linked to the Ayurvedic tradition of marma (vital-point) therapy. The teacher is called a Gurukkal.

 

• Kalaripayattu is believed to have influenced the movement vocabulary of Kathakali and other performing arts of Kerala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indian martial art forms and their home states:

◦ Thang-Ta and Sarit Sarak — Manipur; Thang-Ta is a martial dance using the sword (*thang*) and spear (*ta*)

◦ Silambam — Tamil Nadu, a stick-fighting art

◦ Gatka — Punjab, associated with the Sikh tradition

◦ Mardani Khel — Maharashtra, associated with the Marathas

◦ Thoda — Himachal Pradesh, combining archery with dance

◦ Cheibi Gad-ga and Mukna — Manipur

◦ Kushti (Pehlwani) — northern India

 

• Mallakhamb, performed on a vertical wooden pole or rope, is the state sport of Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Home of Silambam, the stick-fighting art, and of Jallikattu, the bull-taming sport.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for Kambala, the buffalo race, and for the folk theatre form Yakshagana.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): Home of Thang-Ta, and also the birthplace of modern polo (Sagol Kangjei).

question: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched by the Government of India in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Make in India initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. (मेक इन इंडिया — 2014 में शुरू)

 

• Its objectives are to make India a global manufacturing hub, to raise the share of manufacturing in GDP, to create employment, and to promote foreign direct investment and ease of doing business. It initially covered 25 sectors, later expanded to 27.

 

• The initiative rests on four pillars — new processes, new infrastructure, new sectors and a new mindset — and its logo is a lion made of gears.

 

• Make in India 2.0 focuses on sectors including automobile components, aviation, biotechnology, defence manufacturing, electronic systems, pharmaceuticals, railways, renewable energy, textiles and food processing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related national initiatives and their launch years:

◦ Digital India, Skill India and Swachh Bharat Mission — 2014-15

◦ Startup India and Stand Up India — 2016

◦ Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan — 2020

◦ Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes — from 2020

◦ PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan — 2021

 

• Industries are classified by bulk and weight into heavy industries, which use heavy and bulky raw materials and produce heavy goods — such as iron and steel, shipbuilding, automobiles and heavy machinery — and light industries, which use light raw materials to make consumer goods, such as electric bulbs, watches, sewing machines and paint brushes.

 

NOTE

 

• 2012 (Option 1), 2016 (Option 3) and 2019 (Option 4) are incorrect. 2016 was the launch year of Startup India and 2019 of PM-KISAN and the Maandhan pension schemes.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The Vice-President of India is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament, whereas the President is elected by an electoral college which, in addition to the elected members of both Houses, also includes ______.
option_1: the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and of Delhi and Puducherry
option_2: the members of the State Legislative Councils
option_3: the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts
option_4: the elected members of the Panchayati Raj institutions
solution_text:
The correct answer is the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and of Delhi and Puducherry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 54, the President is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

◦ the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, and

◦ the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, and of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry (added by the 70th Amendment, 1992)

 

  (राष्ट्रपति का निर्वाचक मंडल — अनुच्छेद 54)

 

• Nominated members of either House of Parliament or of a State Assembly, and the members of State Legislative Councils, do not take part in the Presidential election.

 

• The Vice-President, under Article 66, is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament — including nominated members — and no State legislators participate.

 

• Both elections are held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and the voting is by secret ballot.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The value of the vote of an MLA = (population of the State as per the 1971 Census ÷ total number of elected members of the Assembly) ÷ 1,000. The value of the vote of an MP = total value of the votes of all MLAs of all States ÷ total number of elected members of Parliament.

 

• Qualifications: the President must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age and be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha; the Vice-President must be qualified for election to the Rajya Sabha.

 

• The Governor, by contrast, is neither elected nor chosen by the State Assembly — he is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President, under Articles 155 and 156.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Members of State Legislative Councils have no role in either election.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The judiciary takes no part in these elections; the Supreme Court only decides disputes arising out of them.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Panchayati Raj members are not part of any electoral college for these offices.

question: How many of the world's recognised biodiversity hotspots extend into India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Four of the world's biodiversity hotspots extend into India: (भारत में चार जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट)

◦ The Himalaya — covering the entire Indian Himalayan region

◦ Indo-Burma — covering the North East, excluding Assam and the Andaman Islands

◦ The Western Ghats and Sri Lanka — the Western Ghats of peninsular India

◦ Sundaland — which includes the Nicobar group of islands

 

• The concept of a biodiversity hotspot was proposed by the British ecologist Norman Myers in 1988. To qualify, a region must satisfy two criteria:

◦ it must contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants found nowhere else (endemics), and

◦ it must have lost at least 70 per cent of its original natural vegetation

 

• There are 36 biodiversity hotspots in the world at present.

 

• India is one of the world's 17 megadiverse countries, and holds about 8 per cent of the world's recorded species on about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Western Ghats are among the world's eight "hottest hotspots" and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012). The threats to their endemic species include habitat loss, infrastructure projects such as roads, dams and mining, forest fires and human-wildlife conflict, and the spread of invasive alien species such as *Lantana camara*, *Prosopis juliflora* and the African catfish.

 

• India's first biosphere reserve was the Nilgiri (1986). Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992.

 

• The principal legislation is the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, under which the National Biodiversity Authority at Chennai was set up.

 

NOTE

 

• Two (Option 1), Three (Option 2) and Six (Option 4) are incorrect. The commonest error is to omit Sundaland, which enters India only through the Nicobar Islands, and so to answer "three".

question: Which Indian satellite, launched in 2015, is a dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory studying celestial sources in the X-ray, optical and ultraviolet bands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AstroSat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• AstroSat, launched on 28 September 2015 by a PSLV-C30, is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory. It observes celestial sources simultaneously in the X-ray, optical and ultraviolet bands — a capability that made it unique among space observatories at the time. (एस्ट्रोसैट — भारत की पहली अंतरिक्ष वेधशाला)

 

• It was placed in a near-equatorial low Earth orbit at about 650 km, and carries five payloads, including the Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (UVIT), the Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT), the Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter (LAXPC), the Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager (CZTI) and the Scanning Sky Monitor (SSM).

 

• Its scientific goals include the study of binary star systems, black holes, neutron stars, active galactic nuclei and the detection of new transient X-ray sources.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian space science missions:

◦ Aditya-L1 (2023) — India's first solar mission, placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1, about 1.5 million km from the Earth

◦ Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Chandrayaan-2 (2019) and Chandrayaan-3 (2023) — lunar missions

◦ Mangalyaan (2013) — the Mars Orbiter Mission, which made India the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt

◦ XPoSat (2024) — a mission to study the polarisation of cosmic X-rays

 

• NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint earth-observation mission placed in a polar sun-synchronous orbit, designed to map changes in the Earth's surface using dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar.

 

NOTE

 

• Aditya-L1 (Option 2): Studies the Sun, particularly the corona and solar wind, and was launched in 2023.

 

• Cartosat (Option 3): A series of Indian earth-observation satellites used for cartography and high-resolution imaging.

 

• Oceansat (Option 4): A series of satellites for the study of ocean and atmospheric parameters, such as sea-surface winds and chlorophyll concentration.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Governor of a State is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

2. A person must have completed thirty-five years of age to be eligible for appointment as Governor.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. Under Article 155, the Governor of a State is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, and under Article 156 he holds office during the pleasure of the President. His normal term is five years, but this is subject to the pleasure of the President, so there is no security of tenure. (राज्यपाल — राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नियुक्त)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Under Article 157, a person to be eligible for appointment as Governor must be a citizen of India and must have completed the age of thirty-five years.

 

• Two conventions are followed in the appointment: the Governor should ordinarily be an outsider, that is, not a resident of the State concerned, and the Chief Minister of the State should be consulted. Neither is a legal requirement.

 

• A Governor may be transferred from one State to another, and may be reappointed. He continues in office beyond the five-year term until his successor enters upon office. The same person may be appointed Governor of two or more States.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Governor can dissolve the State Legislative Assembly on the advice of the Council of Ministers, and in certain circumstances at his discretion. Similarly, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85 — so the two offices are alike in this respect.

 

• Discretionary powers of the Governor include the reservation of a Bill for the consideration of the President, the recommendation of President's Rule under Article 356, the appointment of a Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority, and administration of adjoining Union Territories where he is also the administrator.

 

• The Sarkaria Commission and the Punchhi Commission both examined the office of the Governor and recommended safeguards to insulate it from political pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.
